signature: “IOHANN ((*)) IOSEPH ((*)) SCHMIED ((*)) IN ((*)) PFAFFENDORFF ((*)) 1789 (((*)))”, festoon pattern
pitch: With slide fully closed, E-natural, slightly flat.
mouthpiece: Probably not orig.; very flat rim, funnel-shaped cup; le 102, bowl diam. 33.3 ext., 22.5 int.; depth of bowl 18, throat 4.8 (difficult to measure), mp exit 8.8 int.
dimensions: bo 10.4, mp rcvr 12.15, slide sec. exit 9.6, slide sec. 1930.5, bell sec. 716, overlap 43.5, le 1887, be 110.5 (measured by the author 2/12/99).
provenance: Moravian tradition suggests that the four Schmied (Schmidt) trombones in Gnadenhutten--17891, 17892, 17893, and 1804—were acquired from Lititz when that community purchased a new set.
literature: : van den Bosch 1989: 54; Heyde 1997:102. ****Hartzell? [check other GN insts.]
remarks: Very nice, clear sound in first position; slide too stiff for practical use.Good condition; six ferrules, with ring pattern, in slide sec.; ring pattern also on both slide stays;  X on ferrule at top of immoveable slide stay matches X on ferrule at top of moveable slide stay (intended to show proper alignment of slide); immoveable slide stay not telescopic;  saddle in slide bow (with zigzag pattern on periphery and in center), with sheet-metal style ring (4.7 side, 7 diam.), flat guard on slide bow (perhaps later addition) covers bottom of saddle,  lyre mount attached to immoveable slide stay, slide sprung,  flat bell stay (no eyelet) with zigzag pattern around periphery and in distinctive pattern in center, saddle on bell bow with ring matches slide bow; flat guard on bell bow covers termination of saddle; fairly sharp terminal flare in bell. 17891 17892 and 17893 constitute a set; the soprano trombone 1804, by Johann Joseph Schmied’s son Johann Simon Schmidt, was undoubtedly used with the three 1789 instruments
